items.text: Delirium of the Dying
Forest Near the Field Hospital
Shovels rise and fall as dirt is flung over shoulders.
Soldiers, their eyes forever closed, wait off to the side.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: A rare moment of peace. Is this truly how you wish to spend this time?

items.speaker: Franz
items.text: I'm not just doing this for you. Besides, I told you yesterday not to be so damn polite.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Apologies.

items.speaker: Franz
items.text: You've picked a nice spot for a cemetery.

items.speaker: Franz
items.text: Place hasn't been hit yet—still feels like summer.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: The front may move in this direction soon enough.

items.speaker: Franz
items.text: True. The soldiers you've buried might end up blasted to bits in the shelling—or lying above the mud again.

items.speaker: Franz
items.text: Like ... what's that word again? Sloughs?

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Yes, sloughs.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: It doesn't matter. Once the shells stop falling, I will return and bury them again.

items.speaker: Franz
items.text: Then your work'll never be finished.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: I don't mind.

items.speaker: Franz
items.text: Well, I'd rather spend my time thinking about how I'm going to swipe myself a roast goose.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: ... Many ask me why I continue this task, but never you.

items.speaker: Franz
items.text: There's nothing to ask, Charon. The rookies are banging their heads on the air raid shelter walls, and the veterans are scrounging for cigarettes.

items.speaker: Franz
items.text: Just living another day is good enough for me. Who cares about "why"?

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: ... Indeed.
Charon stops. There's a woman in the distance making her way toward him, a medical bag under her arm.
The trees behind cast a shadow, hiding her face from him.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: But some must search for meaning, or they cannot live.

items.speaker: Franz
items.text: Who's the Schwester?

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: Hello.

items.speaker: Franz
items.text: Tag, Fräulein. Do you know our Charon here?

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: Yes, Herr Schreyer.
The unexpected address causes Franz to rub his chin. Partita turns her gaze to Charon.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: I'll be helping you bury the soldiers.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: It is too dangerous. The field hospital withdrawal is certain to keep you busy enough.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: Lieutenant Colonel Wolker gave me permission. You've got a habit of digging up men who are somehow still alive, it seems.

items.speaker: Franz
items.text: You can't argue with that.
Charon lowers his head and returns to his task in silence.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: You were never good at lying. That's why you won't even talk about Walter.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: Why won't you tell me?

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: It was shellfire. Dust flew everywhere, and then he was gone ... in the blink of an eye.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: That's not the whole story. I know it.
Her conviction leaves Charon speechless.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: First you dodge all my questions, and now you won't even say a word.

items.speaker: Franz
items.text: Fräulein, Charon's mind works a little slower than most. He might just be taking it all in still.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: I see.
She sets down her medical bag and picks up a nearby shovel.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: So, you're a man of action now, are you?
Visibly unsettled, Franz also chooses to remain silent.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: Fine. Then, I'll keep shoveling right here with you until you tell me the truth.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: There is no truth to tell.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: Then it looks like there's nothing for us to talk about. Time to get back to it, action man.
As the grave takes shape, Partita makes her way to the cart, Franz following behind.
Together, they carefully lift one of the bodies.
A cough, faint and abrupt. The three of them glance at each other, and Partita looks toward the cart.

items.speaker: Franz
items.text: Wait, wait, wait ...
Among the many faces piled on the cart, Partita finds one with a little color in its cheeks and gently lifts an eyelid.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: ... Mein Gott! He's alive ... He's still alive!

items.speaker: Franz
items.text: Good grief ... I thought we'd checked them all!
She rushes to her medical bag.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: Quick, move the bodies off him!

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: Be careful, Franz. He might have broken bones.

items.speaker: Partita
items.text: Paul! Don't just stand there! Help us!
Lines from the journal's first pages surface in his mind.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Coming.
The injured soldier who cheated death has been seen to.
Charon stands, still and silent among the beds and stretchers. The cries of the wounded surround him.
Partita vanishes behind a screen, hard at work. Franz motions for Charon to move along.
Charon averts his gaze from the mangled limbs, nods to Franz, and makes to leave.
Paul!
A haggard hand brushes his coat, then falls back, powerless.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: What?
Paul ... Gott im Himmel, finally, someone I know.
Where's Willi? Go fetch him, quick ... He doesn't know I'm in the field hospital.
The soldier's words crackle from his dry throat. His dog tag reads "Fabien."

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: You are Fabien?

items.speaker: Fabien
items.text: Come on, Paul, I'm not already some nameless patient to you, am I?
Deprived too long of familiar company, Fabien has grown talkative—to an oddly feverish degree.

items.speaker: Fabien
items.text: Never mind. Anna will remember me no matter what. I just have to get my discharge, and then we'll go home together.

items.speaker: Fabien
items.text: Anna promised she'd make me a wreath of Ginster when we saw each other again ...

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Who is it you're looking for?

items.speaker: Fabien
items.text: Anna! I want to see Anna—I'll write to her, and she'll come for me. I know she will.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: There was another. Your comrade from the front, perhaps.

items.speaker: Fabien
items.text: I just want to see Anna.
As Charon tries to make sense of his rambling, a doctor walking by shoots him a look.

items.speaker: Doctor
items.text: Best not to take what he says too seriously.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Why?

items.speaker: Doctor
items.text: He rambles like that every day. Wound's not looking good, either.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: What happened to him?

items.speaker: Doctor
items.text: Lost a leg.

items.speaker: Fabien
items.text: You think I can't hear you whispering about me, Doctor! Stop talking rubbish!

items.speaker: Fabien
items.text: Paul, don't believe him—he's just grouchy 'cause I won't call him "Herr."

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: He spoke no ill of you, Fabien—simply discussed today's lunch options.
Fabien drops his gaze, muttering something under his breath. Charon turns and lowers his voice.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Will he live?
The doctor, seemingly irritated with his own misplaced concern, lowers his gaze to the medical file.

items.speaker: Doctor
items.text: It's hard to say. Three days from now, we'll be evacuated to the rear. He'll receive better treatment then.

items.speaker: Doctor
items.text: But if his condition worsens before then, we'll have to leave him behind.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Leave him—with some painkillers.

items.speaker: Doctor
items.text: Yes. We're all preparing to evacuate. Frankly, I doubt he'll last that long.

items.speaker: Doctor
items.text: ... Perhaps it's cold of me to say, but death's just part of the routine here. One bed empties, another fills, and the dog tags pile up like cigarette butts.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: ... Understood.
The doctor gestures to Fabien with his clipboard.

items.speaker: Doctor
items.text: You can see him off, though I imagine you do that for everyone left behind, yes?
Fabien's murmuring begins to fade, then he gasps for breath, like he's choking back a sob.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Yes.
